papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but their immense size and computational requirements hinder their deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to enable complex distributed learning paradigms like federated learning on heterogeneous devices. Advanced methods leverage multiple teachers to improve knowledge transfer, and innovative approaches even permit distillation without access to the original training data. Furthermore, the technique can be adapted to various model architectures, including generative networks, and can be used to improve the interpretability of complex deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Paradigm for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, more efficient models that retain a significant portion of the original model's performance, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in this field have expanded its application beyond simple compression, with methods developed for distilling knowledge from intermediate features, ensembles of teachers, and even in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its successful application in numerous areas, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements for inference, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, while preserving high performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to numerous advancements and specialized methods to improve the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process involves a smaller "student" model learning from a larger "teacher" model, transferring knowledge beyond simple labels. Originally conceived for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Research shows that distillation not only reduces model size and inference time but can also enhance the student model's performance, sometimes even surpassing models trained from scratch. Advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation further broaden its utility, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and effective deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and performance improvement. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. Traditionally, this is achieved by using the teacher's softened output probabilities as supervisory signals for the student. However, recent advancements have explored mimicking intermediate feature representations, which can provide richer information. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending to compressing large language models, improving low-precision networks, and enabling collaborative training in privacy-sensitive settings like federated learning. Furthermore, research challenges the conventional view of a superior teacher guiding a weaker student, suggesting that the regularization effect of the process is a key component of its success, even leading to teacher-free distillation frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Strategy for Compressing Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact "student" model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process transfers the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. By reducing computational and memory requirements, knowledge distillation facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge hardware. Its applications span numerous fields, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its broad utility and effectiveness in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance optimization in deep learning. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Various strategies have been developed, including distilling knowledge from the teacher's final outputs, internal feature representations, or an ensemble of multiple teachers. This methodology has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and federated learning, to create compact, fast, and effective models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to address specific challenges, such as transferring adversarial robustness, performing distillation without access to original training data, mitigating biases, and improving the interaction between teacher and student models.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model. The student network is trained to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while having a significantly smaller footprint. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing models like BERT, as well as in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and medical image segmentation. Advanced methods have been developed to address challenges like under-fitting and to enable distillation without access to the original training data, further extending the technique's applicability and utility.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process aims to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The fundamental idea is to train the student model to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels. This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for compression but also to improve the performance and generalization of the student model.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression and training paradigm in which a compact 'student' model learns to mimic a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from the high-performing teacher to the student, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur in various forms, from mimicking the teacher's final output probabilities (soft labels) to replicating its intermediate feature representations. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image classification. Advanced distillation frameworks include using ensembles of teachers, adversarial training schemes, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own past predictions. Furthermore, knowledge distillation is a key enabler for collaborative learning paradigms like federated learning, allowing knowledge transfer between heterogeneous devices.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different data modalities. However, the process is not without challenges, as student models can struggle with optimization and may inherit undesirable biases from their teachers. Ongoing research focuses on developing more effective distillation strategies, such as using multiple teachers, applying data augmentation, and mitigating fairness issues to create smaller, faster, and more robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer paradigm where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large deep learning models, such as those used in natural language processing (NLP), on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from the teacher, often in the form of soft label probabilities, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. Various strategies have been developed, including data-free distillation, self-distillation, and multi-teacher approaches, extending its application to diverse tasks like machine translation, object detection, and question answering.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for tasks ranging from text generation to image classification. The core principle involves transferring the knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal representations to the student. Advanced variations of this technique have emerged, such as data-free distillation for scenarios with private data, self-distillation where a model learns from itself, and ensemble distillation using multiple teachers. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and create more efficient and generalizable models.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in real-world applications by training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While primarily used to create lightweight yet powerful models that are significantly faster at inference, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further. The technique can be used to transfer beneficial inductive biases between different model architectures, improve algorithmic fairness by mitigating biases against protected groups, and facilitate domain adaptation by transferring knowledge from source domains to a new target domain. By enabling the creation of efficient, robust, and versatile models, knowledge distillation serves as a crucial tool in the practical application of deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger "teacher" model. This process enables the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple size reduction, distillation can transfer inductive biases, improve performance on downstream tasks, and enhance model efficiency across various domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph learning. The framework is highly adaptable, extending to scenarios involving ensemble models, self-improvement, and addressing broader concerns such as data privacy and algorithmic fairness, making it a cornerstone of modern machine learning engineering.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision, have grown increasingly large and computationally expensive, hindering their deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions and internal representations, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart but with significantly lower computational and memory requirements. This approach has demonstrated success across a wide array of tasks, from question answering and object detection to generative modeling, making it a critical tool for creating practical, deployable deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Over time, techniques have evolved beyond simple output matching to include methods based on intermediate features, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning. These advanced approaches have demonstrated success across a wide range of tasks and domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative modeling, making knowledge distillation a critical tool for operationalizing state-of-the-art deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their immense size and computational requirements pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, especially knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution to this problem. Knowledge distillation is a process where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This allows the student to learn a compressed representation of the teacher's knowledge, resulting in a much smaller and faster model that retains a high level of performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a highly effective and versatile framework for compressing deep learning models, enabling their practical application in diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By leveraging knowledge from a powerful but cumbersome teacher, distillation produces efficient student models that bridge the gap between high performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: The Expanding Role of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning where knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model is transferred to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Originally conceived as a method for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly. This technique not only enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments but also serves as a mechanism to enhance the performance of student models beyond what they could achieve through standard training. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its application across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. Recent advancements have introduced more dynamic and effective distillation frameworks, such as online and self-distillation, and have even leveraged the technique to improve model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance across many fields, but their large size and high computational requirements often hinder their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques aim to address this challenge by creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm that involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a more compact 'student' model. This process allows the student model to achieve performance comparable to the teacher while having a significantly smaller footprint. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to handle various scenarios, including using multiple teachers, transferring knowledge across different data modalities, and applying distillation in distributed learning frameworks. These techniques are crucial for enabling the practical use of powerful deep learning models in production systems.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique in deep learning, initially conceived as a method for model compression. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model, enabling the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. It serves as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and increasing the interpretability of opaque "black-box" models. By leveraging the rich, nuanced information captured by teacher models, knowledge distillation can guide student models to achieve superior accuracy, sometimes even surpassing their teachers, and can transform complex neural networks into simpler, more transparent structures like decision trees. This makes it a versatile and indispensable tool in the modern deep learning and natural language processing toolkit.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Initially conceived for model compression, this technique enables the development of lightweight, efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts. Beyond creating faster and smaller models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a crucial tool for a range of tasks including domain adaptation, where models must adjust to new data distributions, and federated learning, which facilitates collaborative training across distributed devices with heterogeneous models without sharing private data. The success of distillation often depends on sophisticated strategies that go beyond simple output matching, such as aligning intermediate feature representations and leveraging statistically sound data augmentation. Despite its power, challenges in optimization remain, but knowledge distillation continues to be a versatile and impactful framework in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight "student" deep learning models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful "teacher" models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. The methods for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more sophisticated techniques that focus on mimicking intermediate feature representations. Innovations in the field include adversarial training frameworks, the application of automated machine learning for architecture search, and even teacher-free approaches that leverage self-distillation as a form of regularization. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant success across a wide range of applications, including the compression of large language models in natural language processing, the simplification of complex graph neural networks, and the optimization of models in federated learning and speech recognition systems.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create compact and efficient neural networks. This technique involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, this approach reduces computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning, using a range of methods from mimicking output probabilities to distilling internal representations and employing adversarial learning frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Approach for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. The technique has found wide-ranging applications across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare, demonstrating its flexibility in creating models that are not only smaller and faster but also sometimes more interpretable or robust.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, which is often encoded in its output probabilities, to the student. This allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices or applications with strict latency requirements. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning. Beyond simple model compression, distillation has been shown to improve the accuracy of student models, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable training even when the original data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by significantly reducing their size and computational footprint while retaining high performance. The core idea involves training the student model to replicate the teacher's output probabilities, which contain richer information than simple class labels. Advanced methods also involve distilling knowledge from the teacher's intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers, or even operating without access to the original training data. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, speech recognition, computer vision, and for improving model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments becomes a significant challenge. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for this purpose. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while maintaining a much smaller footprint. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements for inference, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, while preserving high performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to numerous advancements and specialized methods to improve the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact "student" network learns from a larger "teacher" network. This technique facilitates the deployment of complex deep learning models in settings with limited computational resources. The process involves transferring knowledge through various mechanisms, including mimicking the teacher's final outputs, aligning intermediate feature representations, or preserving relational knowledge. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Beyond simple compression, this framework can be used for more advanced purposes, including transferring specific properties like adversarial robustness or inductive biases between different model architectures. It also enables novel applications like cross-modal learning and improving models in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Task Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Its primary application is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The utility of knowledge distillation extends across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models and computer vision for tasks like object detection and generative modeling. Advanced strategies have also been developed, such as task-adaptive compression, data-free distillation, and online learning frameworks, showcasing the versatility and ongoing evolution of this technique.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, including the nuanced probability distributions over classes, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the ground-truth labels alone. This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and smaller.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, cumbersome models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This teacher-student learning paradigm involves training a compact student model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced relationships between classes, to the student, enabling it to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision, facilitating the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and in specialized environments like federated learning. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a potent regularization technique and a method for enhancing model performance and enabling novel cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, cumbersome 'teacher' model, making it feasible to deploy state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond mere compression. It serves as a flexible framework for transferring knowledge to enhance model accuracy, enable continuous learning across sequential tasks, facilitate domain adaptation without source data, and even improve performance in multi-task learning settings. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a critical tool for advancing the practical application and capabilities of modern neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, state-of-the-art deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve performance far exceeding what it could by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven effective across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, enabling the practical application of otherwise computationally prohibitive models. The methodology extends beyond simple output imitation, with advanced techniques focusing on transferring internal representations and adapting the teaching process itself to further enhance student performance and generalization.
